says: In our tooling, L4 of the Reflect ban (oxlint-plugins/advice.test.ts:850-851 and :892, and field/runs/2026-11-18-reflect-fold-tests1.json) says its stem samples meet a glob for a folder with no tracked code file, but a stem with a wildcard or a brace is skipped (:899) or written as a literal folder, so a JSON.parse warn-block glob that reaches a real fire and also a folder no tracked file has passes every law and makes that new folder's JSON.parse advise; oxlint-plugins/README.md:1219 names only a file kind as the limit.
proof: In a scratch clone at a33114a28, each of next/packages/libfabrika/src/{node,newdir}/** and next/packages/libfabrika/src/n*/** added to the warn block's files leaves L4 green (vitest -t 'Reflect ban L4': 1 passed); node:path matchesGlob holds each on next/packages/libfabrika/src/node/dev/dev.ts, so stale() names neither; oxlint with the planted config grades a JSON.parse in a new src/newdir/x.ts and src/nexus/x.ts 'warning', where the head config grades both 'error'.
cost: The comment and README state the limit narrower than it is, so a later reviewer may trust L4 for a wildcard or brace folder glob; the escape bites only when such a new folder's first file carries a JSON.parse.
